title: Present Continuous Tense (Español (Spanish))
description: [Preview] This content was translated statically to Español (Spanish).
explanation: [Auto Translate Demo] The Present Continuous tense is used to describe actions that are in progress right now (at the moment of speaking) or temporary situations. (This represents side-by-side localized content: Español (Spanish))
keyRules: • Uses: Actions happening now, temporary habits, or current trends. (Español (Spanish) Guide)
• Negative: Subject + am/is/are + not + verb-ing. (Español (Spanish) Guide)

quiz.question: [Español (Spanish)] Complete the sentence: "Listen! The birds ________ in the garden."
quiz.explanation: [Español (Spanish) Explanation] "Birds" is plural, so we use the auxiliary "are" + "singing".

quiz.question: [Español (Spanish)] What is the correct negative form of: "He is doing his homework"?
options: He is not do his homework. (Español (Spanish))
quiz.explanation: [Español (Spanish) Explanation] To form the negative, insert "not" after the auxiliary verb "is" (is not = isn't).

quiz.question: [Español (Spanish)] Identify the present continuous sentence:
options: I go to school every day. (Español (Spanish))
The sun is shining beautifully today. (Español (Spanish))
We enjoyed our trip to Tokyo last year. (Español (Spanish))
You will pass the English exam easily. (Español (Spanish))
quiz.explanation: [Español (Spanish) Explanation] "The sun is shining" fits the [Subject + is + verb-ing] structure describing an action in progress.
